Northlight\'s compass and light tools work on your phone with no account, analytics, or advertising SDKs. An optional Pro purchase is handled by Google Play; Northlight never sees or stores your payment details.
Northlight asks for camera access only when you choose the LED lantern, SOS signal or Pro strobe. Android requires that permission to control the camera flash. It never takes photos or records video.

The compass uses your phone\'s orientation sensors and shows magnetic north. Accuracy can be affected by magnets, metal objects, and some phone cases. Move your phone in a figure-eight if it needs calibration.

Spoken compass is free. It describes the direction your phone points toward magnetic north, not the direction you are walking. Hold the phone flat with its top edge pointing ahead.

Automatic announcements require a stable change of at least 15 degrees and respect your selected minimum interval. Calibration and accuracy warnings replace unreliable directions. Speech stops when you leave Northlight and never restarts automatically.

Northlight uses an installed offline voice in English or Romanian, matching the app language. It does not use your microphone, record audio, or send headings to a speech server. Installing voice data in Android settings may require internet access. With a screen reader active, use Speak direction for a single reading through the screen reader; automatic app speech is disabled.

This is not a navigation or safety aid. It cannot detect obstacles, plan safe routes, or tell you when to cross a road. Keep surrounding sounds audible and do not rely on it for safety-critical decisions.

Northlight uses your phone\'s GPS location only to show altitude while this screen is open. Choose precise location for this optional feature. Your coordinates and altitude are not saved, uploaded, or used for tracking. No background location is requested.\n\nThe compass, lights and spoken compass do not need location access. After allowing access, tap Start GPS altimeter to begin. You can stop it at any time.
Android settings could not be opened. Use your phone\'s Settings to enable location and precise location access for Northlight.

The free altimeter uses GPS / GNSS satellites through Android, not an online elevation service. It starts only when you choose Start GPS altimeter and allow precise location. It stops when you leave this screen or lock the phone, and never restarts on its own. Continuous GPS uses extra battery. No coordinates, routes or altitude history are saved or uploaded. Only your unit preference and permission-request history are saved.

The reference is shown beside the reading. If Android supplies mean-sea-level altitude, that is used. Otherwise the reading is height relative to the WGS84 reference ellipsoid, which can differ from sea level. It is not height above the ground. This version does not use a barometer or weather-based calibration.

Metres and feet show the same estimate in different units. Vertical accuracy is the uncertainty reported for that altitude reference, at 68% confidence, not a guaranteed error limit. Horizontal GPS accuracy is never substituted for vertical accuracy. If vertical accuracy is missing, it is marked unknown. Readings older than about 15 seconds, missing altitude and simulated locations are hidden rather than shown as zero.

GPS may work without mobile data, but needs usable satellite reception; an open view of the sky helps. The compass, lights and spoken compass remain available without location permission. Do not rely on altitude for climbing, aviation, rescue or other safety-critical decisions.

Pro spoken guidance compares your phone's magnetic heading with a saved direction. It says the target direction and how far to turn your phone left or right. Saved bearings are directions, not places. This feature does not use GPS or location permission. Hold the phone flat with its top edge pointing ahead.

Speak guidance requests one current instruction. Automatic guidance waits for a stable heading, then announces alignment changes, left/right changes, or changes of at least 10 degrees in the remaining turn. It respects the selected minimum interval. Stable alignment is recognized within 3 degrees; it is kept until the error exceeds 6 degrees to reduce chatter. There are no constant reminders when nothing changes.

Vibrate on alignment is off by default. When enabled, a reliable, stable aligned reading can produce one short native haptic cue. Turn more than 8 degrees away to rearm it; cues are at least 5 seconds apart. It respects Android haptic settings and depends on phone hardware. It does not vibrate on unreliable readings and never means a route is clear or that you have arrived anywhere.

Low accuracy, calibration needs, stale readings or missing sensors replace turn instructions with warnings. Pause speech, changing or clearing the target, losing Pro access, leaving this screen or locking the phone stops automatic guidance. It never restarts on its own, including after rotation. Voice failure or audio interruption also pauses it.

The installed offline voice, speed and interval settings are shared with the free spoken compass. No microphone, recordings, background guidance or speech server is used. Saved names are not spoken; prompts identify the target by direction and degrees. With a screen reader active, automatic app speech is disabled; use Speak guidance for a single instruction through that reader.

This describes phone orientation only. It cannot plan routes, detect obstacles, tell you where you are, or say when it is safe to cross a road. Keep surrounding sounds audible and never rely on these instructions or vibrations for safety-critical decisions.
